title: Molecular dynamics simulation-based investigation of LexA-DNA interaction: affinity-dependent conformational changes and implications for DNA looping
one_liner_zh: 该文通过全原子分子动力学模拟研究细菌转录因子LexA与不同亲和力DNA基序结合时的构象变化与DNA弯曲机制，精准聚焦TF-DNA互作动态机理，方法为物理模拟，高度匹配本课题。
abstract: Context The binding of proteins to the DNA plays a crucial role in various cellular processes including gene expression. LexA is a bacterial transcription factor that binds to a specific DNA motif, leading to the regulation of numerous genes involved in the DNA damage response. Understanding the structural dynamics and mechanisms of DNA binding by LexA can provide valuable insights into its function and regulatory capabilities. Here, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are used to investigate how the sequence of the DNA binding motif influences the conformational changes and bending behavior of DNA upon LexA binding. Simulation trajectories reveal that the DNA fragment containing a higher affinity LexA binding motif exhibits more pronounced bending and structural deformations compared to that containing a lower affinity binding motif. Additionally, bending of the protein itself is also observed in the presence of the DNA fragment with the higher affinity LexA binding motif. Our results confirm previous reports of LexA-induced DNA bending and shed further light on the structural details of the DNA bending mechanisms. Methods MD simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between LexA and 70 bp-long DNA fragments that differ in the LexA binding motif. The GROMACS simulation package with the AMBER14SB force field for proteins and the AMBERparmbsc1 force field for nucleic acids is used to conduct 100 ns-long all-atom simulations. The solvent is set up with the TIP3P water model and the simulation box is filled with ions to reach 0.15 M salt concentration.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质与DNA的结合在包括基因表达在内的多种细胞过程中起着关键作用。LexA是一种细菌转录因子，它结合到特定的DNA基序上，从而调控参与DNA损伤反应的众多基因。理解LexA与DNA结合的结构动力学和机制，可以为其功能和调控能力提供宝贵的见解。在此，采用分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟来研究DNA结合基序的序列如何影响LexA结合时DNA的构象变化和弯曲行为。模拟轨迹显示，含有较高亲和力LexA结合基序的DNA片段，在LexA结合时表现出更显著的弯曲和结构变形，相比之下，含有较低亲和力结合基序的片段则较弱。此外，在存在较高亲和力LexA结合基序的DNA片段时，也观察到蛋白质本身的弯曲。我们的结果证实了先前关于LexA诱导DNA弯曲的报道，并进一步阐明了DNA弯曲机制的结构细节。方法部分采用MD模拟来研究LexA与长度70 bp、且LexA结合基序不同的DNA片段之间的相互作用。使用GROMACS模拟软件包，其中蛋白质采用AMBER14SB力场，核酸采用AMBERparmbsc1力场，进行了100 ns的全原子模拟。溶剂采用TIP3P水模型设置，模拟盒中填充离子以达到0.15 M的盐浓度。
